messages:
marco: Quick question about a half-day move for year-end coverage. My contractor, Nia, has a local observance on 2026-12-31 but we need her for a 2pm interview slot that day. She wants to take a half-day (morning off) on 12/31 and instead take a half-day on 2027-01-04 (afternoon). Is that allowed as a swap or do contractors need a different flow?

june: Short answer: contractors don't accrue PTO like full-time employees, so there's no "carryover" in the accrual sense. We allow one-off schedule swaps for contractors if it's documented and the engagement manager approves. It becomes a timesheet/admin note rather than an accrual/carryover.

marco: OK thanks. So how do we record it so Payroll and Recruiting know shes covering the afternoon panel on 12/31? And does the year-end blackout apply to contractors?

june: Two parts: 1) Year-end blackout applies to headcount scheduling for everyone for critical coverage windows, but contractors are evaluated case-by-case since their hours are flexible. Still, submit before the blackout cutoff so Recruiting can reassign if needed. 2) Record the swap in the People Portal using the "Time-off Adjustment" form and also add a timesheet comment. In practice for contractors pick type: "one-time schedule swap (contractor)". Include manager sign-off and note the hours (e.g., 4h).

talya: Adding payroll detail: because contractors aren't on the accrual system, Payroll needs a clear timesheet entry and a short email documenting the swap so we can reconcile invoices. If the swap spans the payroll cutoff it affects invoicing vs. accruals. Payroll cutoff for year-end processing is 2026-12-20 23:59 UTC — anything after that requiring special handling needs the "manual payroll reconciliation" checkbox on the form.

marco: Got it. Can we use comp time instead of moving the day? We sometimes do comp-off for contractors who do overtime during holiday weeks.

june: We discourage using comp time for contractors unless the contract specifically allows it. For employees, comp time can be logged but must be taken within the quarter. For contractors, route through your vendor manager and Procurement for approval.

marco: What's the exact info to put in the Time-off Adjustment form?

talya: Use these fields in the form:
```
- type: one-time schedule swap (contractor)
- original_date: 2026-12-31 morning (4h)
- new_date: 2027-01-04 afternoon (4h)
- manager_approval: attach email thread
- timesheet_note: "Covering 14:00 interview panel on 2026-12-31; swap approved"
- payroll_reconciliation: yes (if submitted after 2026-12-20)
- coverage_plan: "Recruiting backup: Priya on panel if conflict"
```
Also cc payroll@redwood.example.com in the submission email so they can reconcile the contractor invoice.

marco: Perfect. One more edge case: if Nia's vendor company requires we mark 12/31 as a holiday on their invoice, do we still mark the morning off as unpaid and the Jan 4 afternoon as billed? How to avoid double-billing?

talya: That9s a vendor question but Payroll will coordinate: include vendor name and invoice period on the form, and set payroll_reconciliation=yes. Procurement should confirm billing treatment. We'll create a manual journal entry if needed to avoid double payment.

marco: Submitted the Time-off Adjustment (submitted 2534567920) and attached the manager approval. Added timesheet note and cc'd payroll. Recruiting backup set. Thanks all.

people-ops-bot: Ticket created: HR-5333 (half-day contractor schedule swap). Assigned: June. Reminder: year-end blackout for unscheduled PTO = 2026-12-24 to 2026-12-31 UTC. For contractor exceptions include vendor + invoice details. Link: https://redwood.example.com/hr/year-end
